answer.summary: Duolingo times the practice reminder for 23½ hours after a user’s previous practice, using when they actually practiced rather than a user-set schedule; if they still haven’t extended their streak, it may send a separate reminder at 10 p.m.

sections.heading: Practice reminder
sections.content: Send the reminder 23½ hours after the user practiced the previous day. For example, practice at noon today leads to a reminder at 11:30 a.m. tomorrow. Shuttleworth said they replaced user-set reminder times because actual practice time was a better indicator than when users said they planned to practice. They tested more complex timing logic, but 23½ hours consistently worked best.

sections.heading: Separate late-night reminder
sections.content: Duolingo also sends a distinct “streak saver” at 10 p.m. if the user has not extended their streak, reminding them it is their last chance that day. This is separate from the practice reminder.
